_comment: Every VS Code platform target TierMux ships, and which @vscode/ripgrep package each needs.
Source of truth for BOTH release paths (package-targets.sh and packageAllTargets.mjs), which
previously kept their own lists and had drifted to 6 and 4 targets — publish:all silently
shipped no Linux ARM, Windows ARM or Alpine build at all.
`rg` is NOT the VS Code target name: @vscode/ripgrep/lib/index.js resolves its binary as
`@vscode/ripgrep-${process.platform}-${process.arch}` at RUNTIME, so the directory installed
into a VSIX has to carry that name, not the target's. linux-armhf runs as linux-arm, and both
alpine targets run as plain linux — their rg binaries are statically linked, so the glibc
packages work under musl (verified with file(1) on 1.18.0: static-pie / statically linked).
Getting this wrong is not a soft failure: '@vscode/ripgrep' is external in the bundle, so
Node's real require() runs lib/index.js, which THROWS when the package is absent — the
extension fails to activate. That is also why there is no universal/no-target VSIX.
win32-ia32 is absent on purpose: VS Code dropped 32-bit Windows, so it is no longer a valid
target, even though @vscode/ripgrep still publishes the binary. `web` needs child_process.
